messages:
Nina (PM): Heads-up: Enterprise X wants private deploy with SSO + audit + 99.9 SLA for inference. They want to go live in ~3 weeks. We need owners, risks, and minimal launch criteria.
Mei (CS): Confirmed. They expect strict data residency and an internal compliance questionnaire answered.
Ravi (Eng): Which model and perf baseline? 99.9 SLA at p99 seems tight for large 70B quantized unless we overprovision.
Nina (PM): Model: Orion-70B-q4; baseline from benchmark doc shows p99 ~420ms on our optimized runtime at steady 6 rps. Customer wants spike handling up to 30 rps for short bursts.
Tomas (Runtime): Spike handling needs autoscaling buffer + KV prefix caching. We can sustain short 30 rps bursts if GPU headroom and batching are tuned. Need GPU count estimate.
Ava (Infra): Reserved pool + fast autoscale. Cloud quota check: we might hit reserved-GPU limits in region. I'll start quota request now.
Ibrahim (Security): Audit logs + KMS + SSO. For 99.9 SLA we also need secure fallbacks and cryptographic key rotation policy. Need DF diagram and list of endpoints.
Casey (SRE): Runbook essentials: who flips traffic, how to monitor latency inflation, and explicit rollback to hosted API. Add SLO burn rate alerts.
Ravi (Eng): Proposal: phased rollout using traffic slices: 5% -> 20% -> 60% -> 100% with at-least-15min observation windows. If p99 > 600ms or error > 0.5% during any window, rollback.
Nina (PM): Good. Add explicit acceptance on model quality: perf AND model response similarity to hosted baseline. Legal requires no degradation vs hosted.
Tomas (Runtime): We'll run a regression harness comparing a fixed eval set. Suggest: BLEU/ROUGE-like sim + embedding similarity threshold. I can add automation.
Mei (CS): Customer wants explicit on1pm option later. For now they want VPC + SSO. On1prem may add 4+ weeks.
Ava (Infra): VPC peering + private subnet + NAT + routes — ETA 4 business days after approvals. If we need on1prem later, separate plan.
Ibrahim (Security): Quick blockers: (1) KMS policy draft, (2) audit log retention policy, (3) SSO SCIM provisioning. Who owns KMS policy?
Ravi (Eng): I'll draft KMS policy and sample IAM roles. Link when ready.
Casey (SRE): I'll prepare the canary dashboard and alert thresholds. Can we agree on metrics: p50/p95/p99, error rate, GPU mem usage, queue depth, and tail latency by model context length?
Tomas (Runtime): Yes. Also capture KV cache hit rate and batch size distribution. Those are critical to cost and latency.
Mei (CS): I'll collect the customer's compliance doc and share PII matrix. Also will ask if they can accept a staged SLA ramp (start with 99.5 then 99.9 after 30 days).
Nina (PM): Do we accept staged SLA? That affects contracts. I'll sync with sales/legal.
Ava (Infra): Quota escalated: ticket CLOUD-Q-832. If approved, reserve pool provisioning starts immediately. If denied, fallback is to smaller reserved footprint + autoscale slower.
Ravi (Eng): Engineering risk: if GPU quotas unavailable, we can fall back to a smaller model family (Orion-13B quantized) as a short-term mitigation. Need product approval for feature parity tradeoff.
Ibrahim (Security): Also need to decide log forwarding destination and RBAC for customer access to logs. Customer may require 12-month retention. That increases cost.
Casey (SRE): Runbook drill: Tue 09:00 30m tabletop. We'll simulate regressions and a rollback. deploy-bot, please create invite.
deploy-bot: calendar invite created: "Enterprise X Private Deploy - Runbook Drill" 2024-05-14 09:00
Tomas (Runtime): I'll prototype the regression harness today and post a link. It will run: 
```bash
python tools/regress.py --model orion-70b-q4 --suite enterprise_x_eval.json --samples 500
```
Tomas (Runtime): Pass criteria: median similarity >= 0.95 vs hosted baseline and p99 latency < 700ms during 5min sustained load at target batch config.
Nina (PM): Owners: Nina (program owner), Ravi (engineering lead & KMS policy), Tomas (runtime + regression harness), Ava (infra provisioning), Ibrahim (security signoff), Casey (SRE runbook & alerts), Mei (customer liaison).
Mei (CS): I'll ask customer if they can flexible the SLA ramp or reduce initial burst requirement. That would help.
Ravi (Eng): I'll put up an RFC for the rollout plan and the fallback model path.
Ava (Infra): INFRA-1199 created for VPC + reserved pool.
Ibrahim (Security): SEC-501 created for review. Please attach DF diagram and RBAC proposal.
Casey (SRE): Added runbook stub: https://git.company/runbooks/enterprise_x_private.md
Tomas (Runtime): Perf PR: https://git.company/runtime/perf/pulls/78
Nina (PM): Daily mini updates in this thread until we hit canary. Call out any slips ASAP. Thanks all.
Mei (CS): Noted. Will update customer weekly and flag any blocking contract items.
